stars.passed.why: The assistant gave the right answer.
stars.minimalSet.why: Only the needed skills were used, nothing wasted.

1-1.goal: A customer has just messaged the chat. Build an assistant that greets them warmly and puts them at ease.

constraint.0: The first message should be warm and friendly.

1-2.goal: A customer complained about a late delivery. Build an assistant that replies calmly and politely, in a business tone.

constraint.0: The tone should be measured and respectful, never overly familiar.

1-3.goal: A customer is in a hurry and asks for the shortest possible answer. Build an assistant that keeps it to a couple of sentences.

constraint.0: The reply must be short — no more than two sentences.

1-4.goal: A customer asks about the company. Build an assistant that answers on behalf of the company, not for itself.

constraint.0: The assistant should say “we” on the company's behalf, not “I”.

2-1.goal: A customer asks: “What's the dollar worth in rubles right now?” Build an assistant that gives an up-to-date answer.

constraint.0: The rate changes every day — the answer must be fresh, not from memory.

2-2.goal: A customer sent a list of items and asks for the total estimate. Build an assistant that adds it all up without mistakes.

constraint.0: The estimate has several lines — the total must add up exactly, not by eyeballing.

2-3.goal: A customer asks what the contract says about returns. Build an assistant that finds the right clause in the document itself.

constraint.0: The answer must rely on the contract's text, not on guesswork.

2-4.goal: A manager asks for a short digest of the latest news on a topic. Build an assistant that pulls it from today's sources.

constraint.0: The news must be fresh — from the web, not from memory.

3-1.goal: A customer introduced themselves at the start of the chat. Build an assistant that remembers the name and uses it later.

constraint.0: The name is given once — the assistant must hold on to it through the conversation.

3-2.goal: A customer writes again and refers to an earlier conversation. Build an assistant that recalls what it was about.

constraint.0: The answer must take past conversations into account, not start from scratch.

3-3.goal: A customer asks a frequently asked question. Build an assistant that answers using the FAQ knowledge base.

constraint.0: The answer must draw on the knowledge base, not on vague phrases.

3-4.goal: A customer asks about a detail the assistant doesn't know. Build an assistant that says so honestly instead of making something up.

constraint.0: If the assistant doesn't remember something, it should admit it honestly, not invent an answer.

q0.stem: The assistant replied to a customer too dryly when a warm tone was needed. Why did that happen?

opt.1: It wasn't told what tone to use

q1.stem: You want the assistant to answer briefly, in a couple of sentences. What should you do?

opt.0: Nothing, it will figure it out
opt.2: Simply ask it to keep answers short

q2.stem: A customer complained about a delay. Which tone fits best here?

q3.stem: You need the assistant to answer on the company's behalf, not for itself. What should you tell it?

q4.stem: Two assistants got the very same question but answered quite differently. What most likely caused that?

opt.2: The different roles and instructions they were given

q0.stem: The assistant quoted an out-of-date exchange rate. What did it lack?

q1.stem: You need to add up a long list of figures in an estimate exactly. What's best to give the assistant?

opt.0: A request to add it up in its head

q2.stem: A customer asks what their contract says. What helps the assistant answer accurately?

opt.1: Letting the assistant read the document itself

q3.stem: When does the assistant actually need access to fresh data from the web?

opt.0: When the answer depends on something that changes day to day

q4.stem: The assistant confidently quoted a contract clause that isn't there. How do you avoid that?

opt.1: Give it access to the document itself so it relies on the text

q0.stem: In a new conversation the assistant forgot the customer's name from earlier. What should you add?

q1.stem: A customer refers to an earlier chat, but the assistant says “we haven't met”. What's missing?

q2.stem: You want the assistant to answer common questions from your own materials. What should you give it?

opt.1: A knowledge base of ready-made answers

q3.stem: The assistant doesn't remember a needed detail. What's the best thing for it to do?

opt.2: Honestly say it doesn't have the detail and offer to check

q4.stem: Why does the assistant need memory?

opt.0: To hold on to a name, context, and past conversations

read.thought: The customer has just arrived — a warm welcome is the right move.

reply.done: Greeted the customer warmly and offered to help.

wrong-role.fail: The assistant answered in the wrong voice: instead of a warm welcome it came across as dry. Pick the “Friendly helper” role.

read.thought: The customer is upset — I'll reply calmly and politely, in a business tone.

reply.done: Replied to the complaint politely and with restraint.

wrong-role.fail: The assistant answered in the wrong voice: a complaint needs a measured business tone. Pick the “Business tone” role.

read.thought: The customer is in a hurry — I'll keep it to a couple of sentences.

reply.done: Answered briefly and to the point, in two sentences.

wrong-role.fail: The assistant answered in the wrong voice: it ran on too long. Pick the “Short and to the point” role.

read.thought: A question about the company — I'll answer on its behalf, saying “we”.

reply.done: Answered on behalf of the company, saying “we”.

wrong-role.fail: The assistant answered in the wrong voice: it spoke for itself when it should speak for the company. Pick the “Speaks for the company” role.

need.thought: To name the rate, I need today's data.

fetch.action: Looked up today's dollar rate on the web.
fetch.fail: Couldn't find the answer: no internet access, and the rate needs to be today's. Add the “Web search” skill.

waste.observation: For some reason it opened the calculator and tried to work out the rate itself — a wasted step, you can't get the data that way.

answer.done: Told the customer the current dollar rate.

need.thought: The estimate has several lines — I'll add them up carefully so the total is right.

use.action: Added all the line items on the calculator and got an exact total.
use.fail: Guessed the total in its head and got it wrong: without a calculator the figure doesn't add up. Add the “Calculator” skill.

saw.observation: Checked that the lines add up to the total.

answer.done: Gave the customer the exact estimate total.

need.thought: To answer about returns, I need to look inside the contract itself.

use.action: Opened the contract and found the right clause about returns.
use.fail: Made up a clause that isn't in the contract: without reading the document the answer isn't reliable. Add the “Document reading” skill.

saw.observation: Matched the wording against the contract text.

answer.done: Quoted the customer the exact contract clause.

need.thought: The digest must be fresh — I'll use today's sources from the web.

fetch.action: Gathered the latest news on the topic from the web.
fetch.fail: Couldn't put the digest together: no internet access, and the news needs to be today's. Add the “Web search” skill.

waste.observation: For some reason it opened the calculator — useless for a news digest, just a wasted step.

saw.observation: Picked out the freshest items on the topic.

answer.done: Put together a short digest of the latest news.

need.thought: The customer gave their name — I'll remember it so I can use it later.

recall.action: Remembered the customer's name and used it in the reply.
recall.fail: Asked again for a name the customer had already given: without in-conversation memory it slipped away. Add the “In-conversation memory” skill.

answer.done: Addressed the customer by name and helped with their question.

need.thought: The customer refers to an earlier chat — I'll pull up what it was about.

recall.action: Recalled the past conversation and picked it up where it left off.
recall.fail: Replied “we haven't met”: without memory of past chats the earlier conversation was lost. Add the “Memory of past chats” skill.

answer.done: Took the past conversation into account and helped the customer further.

need.thought: This is a common question — I'll look the answer up in the knowledge base.

recall.action: Found the answer in the FAQ knowledge base and leaned on it.
recall.fail: Answered in vague terms: without a knowledge base there was nothing to lean on. Add the “Knowledge base” skill.

answer.done: Gave the customer a precise answer from the FAQ knowledge base.

recall.thought: They're asking about a detail — I'll check whether I actually remember it.
recall.action: Pulled up the earlier conversation and found the detail.

3-4.refuse: Honestly said it didn't remember that detail and offered to double-check — it didn't make an answer up.

answer.done: Recalled the detail and answered the customer precisely.

diag.missing-tool: The assistant failed: it needed a fresh answer from the web, but had no “Web search” skill. Add it.
diag.no-memory: The assistant failed: it needed to remember something, but had no memory skill. Add the right kind of memory.
diag.budget-exceeded: The assistant got there, but used too many steps. Remove the extra skills.
diag.wrong-role: The assistant answered in the wrong tone. Pick a suitable role.
diag.no-stopping-loop: The assistant got stuck in a loop and didn't stop in time. It needs the “Stopping” skill.
diag.no-guardrail-injection: The assistant fell for a trick in the request. It needs the “Safety” skill.

term.role: A role is the assistant's character and tone: polite, businesslike, brief.
term.web-search: Web search lets the assistant find fresh data online instead of answering from memory.
term.calculator: The calculator does precise math with numbers. It cannot look up data.
term.doc-reader: Document reading lets the assistant read attached files.
term.mem-working: In-conversation memory lets the assistant hold on to details of the current chat: a name, a request, the context.
term.memory: Memory lets the assistant remember past conversations with the customer.
term.mem-semantic: A knowledge base lets the assistant lean on ready-made answers and reference material.
